page_topic_one_liner: AI flashcard tools — active recall and FSRS spaced repetition with AI-generated Q&A from PDFs, lectures, and videos
differentiator_vs_generic: This is science-backed retrieval practice with algorithmic review scheduling — NOT homework photo-to-answer rescue, NOT generic study desk. Hero must be a flashcard flip moment plus spaced repetition timeline on a forgetting curve.
visual_anchors: HERO (~55% canvas): Large tilted flashcard mid-flip — question side visible, answer side peeking, titian-red accent edge; below card: FSRS spaced repetition timeline with 4-5 review dots at expanding intervals along a decay curve
Secondary: source-to-cards pipeline — PDF/lecture doc icon → arrow → stack of auto-generated Q&A card pairs (blurred text)
Tertiary: active recall vs re-read contrast — highlighted textbook faded/X'd vs retrieval checkmark on flashcard
anti_patterns: Generic notebook/highlighter study scene as hero
LLM chat tutor panel as hero
Quiz game leaderboard without flashcard or schedule
Empty card grid with no spacing algorithm visual

en.headline: AI FLASHCARD MAKERS
en.subtitle: Spaced Repetition & Active Recall
en.composition: Visual-only editorial collage for AI flashcard tools guide. HERO: right two-thirds — oversized flashcard at flip angle with blurred Q on front and partial A on back, titian-red card edge; beneath it a forgetting-curve graph with spaced review dots at widening intervals (FSRS schedule visual). Secondary: PDF icon feeding into vertical stack of 3 mini flashcards. Tertiary: faded highlighted notes crossed out vs flashcard with retrieval checkmark. Title block top-left only. Paper torn edges, halftone. NO homework camera UI, NO LLM chat hero, NO real Quizlet branding, NO readable question text on cards, NO leaderboard gamification focus.
